question.problem:
Calculate the value of 
$\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & -2 & 1 \\ 3 & -4 & -1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & -5 & 2 \\ 4 & -3 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}|.$

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries below ${a}_{14}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4\times 4$ determinant to a $3\times 3$ determinant.*
question.worked_solution:
Using elementary row operations, let's make entries below ${a}_{14}=1$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & -2 & 1 \\ 3 & -4 & -1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & -5 & 2 \\ 4 & -3 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+4{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & -2 & 1 \\ 6 & -13 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & -5 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & -7 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & -2 & 1 \\ 6 & -13 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & -5 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & -7 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{1+4}|\begin{aligned}6 & -13 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & -1 \\ 0 & 9 & -7\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}6 & -13 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & -1 \\ 0 & 9 & -7\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot 6\cdot (-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}-5 & -1 \\ 9 & -7\end{aligned}| \\  & =-6(35-(-9)) \\  & =-264.\end{aligned}
$$
